label: input is u/h/q/e/n/v (necessary but not sufficient)
explanation: Token-gated unit. About 95% of activations (96% of mass) occur when the current input is one of u, h, q, e, n, v, with u by far the strongest (40% of mass, 13x lift), then h, e, q. It never fires at t=0 or at the delimiter step, and almost never on other tokens. But only ~5% of steps with these inputs fire, so the token is a necessary gate and the rest depends on context the predicate does not capture. Context that helps: in the copy phase, firing is more likely when the token being output is a, r, o, c or k (out_tok=a gives 7x lift). The strongest activations are on u or e input early in the copy phase when the next output is a (e.g. u a ..., e a ...). Firing rate rises with sequence length and later original positions. No simple context condition raised precision above ~10% without losing most of the recall.
